question.text: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between 'Previous Year' and 'Assessment Year' under the Income Tax Act?

answer.text: Previous Year is the year in which tax return is filed; Assessment Year is the year in which income is earned
Both Previous Year and Assessment Year refer to the same financial year
Previous Year is always a calendar year (January to December) while Assessment Year is a financial year (April to March)
Previous Year is the financial year in which income is earned; Assessment Year is the immediately following financial year in which such income is assessed to tax

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income Tax Act, the "Previous Year" (PY) is the financial year (April to March) in which income is earned or received, and the "Assessment Year" (AY) is the financial year immediately following that PY, during which the income of the PY is assessed to tax and the return is filed. For example, income earned in FY 2025-26 (PY) is assessed in AY 2026-27. The Trap: "PY = year of filing; AY = year of earning" reverses the two definitions. "Both refer to the same financial year" misses the fact that AY always follows PY. "PY is a calendar year while AY is a financial year" is factually wrong — both PY and AY follow the April-to-March cycle under Indian tax law. Note: The cited NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser Level 2 workbook pages use the terms "financial year", "previous year" and "assessment year" in tax-rate and rebate discussions but do not contain a stand-alone definitional statement of the PY-AY relationship at the locations checked. The definition above is presented as general Income Tax Act terminology, not as a workbook-page citation.
